current_subject: spectrum_implementation; selected provider files are pinned in the contract
criterion: Maximum change at every supplied observation pixel <0.1 supplied uncertainty, for each independent refinement and all seven recorded cases. The final candidate also meets the same criterion with all axes refined jointly.
gradient_scope: Five parameter directions (log mass loss, log dilution, top temperature, rotation, zonal speed). Forward/reverse objective derivatives and two finite-difference steps in seven cases; full observer-pixel Jacobian at baseline.
linewidth_scope: A controlled baseline ablation holds populations fixed and changes only natural widths. The difference measures sensitivity to the isolated-transition approximation; it is not a fit or full pressure-broadening validation.
formulation_review: Reviewed intensity/emissivity units per wavenumber, branch Einstein coefficients, both-level lifetime widths including two-photon decay, and infinite-domain Voigt normalization.
Reviewed charge closure, explicit n3 state selection and implicit differentiation of electron-dependent rates. Wind molecular weight and temperature remain prescribed.
Outward radial speed projects as -mu*v. The layer optical depth is vertical; the existing ExoJAX solver divides by mu once. Emission and extinction sum before the source is formed.
Frequency-dependent net extinction is checked on every evaluated ray; no inversion is clipped. Only the separate legacy known-source wrapper admits zero-column vacuum.

All four initial PDF pages and the two changed pages after the final rebuild were visually inspected; no TeX overflow or unresolved references remained. Equation/source review is not an atmospheric validation.
dependency_scope: The initial local ExoJAX tree and final clean revision have distinct manifests. Equal-configuration 64-layer and 128-layer controls give exactly equal observer pixels across consecutive attempts at all seven cases; this is not an equivalence claim for every ExoJAX function.
scientific_limitations: These finite samples do not guarantee resolution or gradients throughout a future prior.
